authority: Native semantics and rollout prerequisite evidence; feature adoption and task qualification remain pending.

nativeEvidence.sourceScope: Recorded Git revision is the experiment base; the newly authored driver is bound by its exact sourceBindings digest. The public copy has identical bytes.

observations: With remote caching, signing and longerSignatureKey enabled, supplied keys shorter than 32 UTF-8 bytes are rejected before task execution. Empty and 31-byte keys are included in the test cases. Bearer and team settings are synthetic.
When longerSignatureKey is absent or false, short supplied keys produce a warning and the task executes.
Sixteen non-ASCII characters encoded as 32 UTF-8 bytes pass the length check. Fifteen of those characters plus one ASCII character are 31 bytes and fail when enforcement is enabled.
A missing key still permits task execution and a later artifact signature warning. Native length enforcement does not replace the Beep role policy for missing keys.
Local execution and execution with signing disabled do not enforce the minimum remote signature key length.

retainedCalibrationFailures: Initial --force and --cache combination was refused before task execution; no signature conclusion was drawn.
Local-only calibration correctly performed no key-length enforcement; this was not treated as remote behavior.

The first commit hook rejected a source checksum stored under a filename used as a map property. The driver now uses explicit path and sha256 source bindings. The same 168 cases were rerun without changing scanner rules.
